html:
The Kathlamet were a Chinookan people of the lower Columbia River, near its mouth, in what is now southwestern Washington and northwestern Oregon. They spoke Kathlamet, a form of the Chinookan language.

They lived in cedar plank houses and fished for salmon, and traded along the river with the Chinook, Clatsop and Wahkiakum. The Lewis and Clark Expedition met them in 1805. Epidemics of the 1830s killed most of the lower Columbia peoples. The Kathlamet language survives mainly through texts that Franz Boas took down in the 1890s from Charles Cultee, one of its last speakers.
